items.summary: Here's a lyric for you: "God’s got a picture of the whole world burning, down to the details of his hot white ash." That's the opening line from Emma Ruth Rundle's new single "God's Picture," and it's also the fantasy at the song's center. Rundle is a master of bleak and heavy mood music, and she'll release her new album These Killing Times in a couple of weeks. We've already heard the early tracks " Powerless " and " Enough ." items.title: Cassandra Wilson, Grammy-winning jazz singer, dies aged 70
items.summary: Mississippi-born Wilson, who worked across folk, pop, R&B and country, was once dubbed America’s best singer Cassandra Wilson, the two-time Grammy-winning jazz singer, songwriter and producer has died. She was 70. Dubbed America’s best singer by Time magazine in 2001, Wilson was best known for her genre-bending voice, which expanded the boundaries of traditional blues-based jazz and worked effortlessly across folk, pop, R&B, country and beyond. At the heart of all her work was her idiosyncratic contralto, a soulful sound distinctly tied to her roots. Continue reading...

items.title: The extraordinary untold story of Freddie Mercury: Mary Austin on her best friend – and love of her life
items.summary: He was Queen’s flamboyant frontman. She was his shy girlfriend, dreaming of marriage until they both realised he preferred men. Thirty-five years after his death, in the week he would have turned 80, Mary Austin talks about their unbreakable bond There were four silver trunks in Mary Austin’s attic that she packed in the mid-1980s and hadn’t opened since.
